summary: Rabies vaccine (human diploid cell vaccine [HDCV], purified chick embryo cell vaccine [PCECV], or purified Vero cell rabies vaccine [PVRV]) provides active immunity against rabies virus infection. It is indicated for post-exposure prophylaxis (PEP) following Category II or III animal exposures and pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP) in individuals at high risk of exposure. Because clinical rabies encephalitis is virtually 100% fatal once symptoms appear, post-exposure prophylaxis has NO absolute contraindications—it must be administered to pregnant women, infants, elderly patients, and immunocompromised individuals. For Category III exposures, rabies immunoglobulin (HRIG 20 IU/kg or ERIG 40 IU/kg) must be co-administered on Day 0.
indications: Post-exposure prophylaxis (PEP) following animal bites, scratches, or contact with saliva on mucous membranes or broken skin (Category II and Category III exposures per WHO/NCDC guidelines)
Post-exposure prophylaxis following bat contact or exposure in rabies-endemic settings
Pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP) for veterinarians, animal handlers, wildlife personnel, laboratory workers handling live rabies virus, and travelers to rabies-endemic regions

dosage.d: 1 full vial (>=2.5 IU) on Days 0, 3, 7, 14, and 28
dosage.n: Deltoid in adults and children >=2 yr; anterolateral thigh in infants <2 yr. NEVER inject into the gluteus (subcutaneous fat reduces seroconversion).

dosage.c: PEP - Updated Thai Red Cross 2-site intradermal regimen (WHO 2018)
dosage.d: 0.1 mL ID at 2 separate anatomical sites (left and right deltoid) on Days 0, 3, and 7
dosage.t: 3 visits, 2 sites per visit (total 6 ID injections)
dosage.n: Cost-effective, dose-sparing regimen widely endorsed by WHO and Government of India (NCDC). Day 14/28 omitted in immunocompetent.

dosage.d: 1 vial IM (or 0.1 mL ID) on Day 0 and Day 3 only
dosage.n: Rabies immunoglobulin (RIG) is NOT indicated in previously vaccinated persons; booster doses trigger rapid anamnestic antibody rise.

dosage.d: 1 vial IM (or 0.1 mL ID) on Days 0, 7, and 21 or 28
dosage.n: Serological testing or booster every 1-2 years for continuous occupational exposure.

admin: Immediate wound toilet is the life-saving first step: thoroughly flush and wash all bite wounds and scratches with soap and running water for at least 15 minutes.
Apply virucidal antiseptic (e.g., povidone-iodine 5% or 70% alcohol) to the wound after thorough washing.

Category III exposure (transdermal bites, scratches with bleeding, licks on broken skin or mucous membranes) requires immediate infiltration of Rabies Immunoglobulin (HRIG 20 IU/kg or ERIG 40 IU/kg) in and around the wound on Day 0.
Administer vaccine strictly IM in the deltoid muscle of the arm (or anterolateral thigh in infants <2 years). NEVER administer in the gluteal/buttock area.
Administer RIG and rabies vaccine at separate anatomical sites using separate syringes.
Avoid suturing bite wounds immediately. If suturing is clinically unavoidable, infiltrate RIG first and apply loose, interrupted sutures.
Tetanus toxoid booster and wound antimicrobial coverage (e.g., amoxicillin-clavulanate) should be evaluated concurrently.
moa: Inactivated rabies virus grown in cell culture (human diploid, chick embryo, or Vero cells) stimulates the host immune system to produce rabies virus-neutralizing antibodies (RVNA, primarily IgG) directed against the viral G-glycoprotein. Protective antibody titers (>=0.5 IU/mL) neutralize the virus at the inoculation site and prevent retrograde axonal transport of rabies virus along peripheral nerves into the central nervous system.

absolute: NONE for post-exposure prophylaxis (PEP). Rabies is virtually 100% fatal once encephalitic symptoms develop; suspected or confirmed exposure mandates complete prophylaxis in ALL individuals regardless of age, pregnancy, or pre-existing medical conditions.
relative: Pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP) only: defer in severe acute febrile illness; documented severe anaphylaxis to prior rabies vaccine dose or component (switch to an alternative cell-culture platform under close clinical monitoring).
monitor: Local injection site pain, erythema, swelling, induration
Transient low-grade fever, headache, myalgia, nausea, dizziness
Very rare neuroparalytic reactions (extremely rare with modern cell-culture vaccines compared to obsolete nerve-tissue vaccines)

preg: Safe & mandatory for PEP. Rabies is 100% fatal; pregnancy or lactation is NEVER a contraindication to post-exposure prophylaxis or rabies immunoglobulin. No adverse teratogenic or fetal outcomes documented.
lact: Safe. Compatible with breastfeeding; vaccination should not be interrupted or delayed.
renal: No dose adjustment required. Complete full schedule. In severe renal failure or hemodialysis, consider measuring neutralizing antibody titers post-completion to verify seroprotection.
serious_se: Urticaria / serum sickness-like type III hypersensitivity (more frequent with booster doses of HDCV)
Transient neurological events (Guillain-Barré syndrome, extremely rare with cell-culture vaccines)
monitoring: Verify patient adherence to mandatory injection dates (Days 0, 3, 7, 14, 28)
Wound inspection for secondary bacterial infection
Observe patient for 15-30 minutes post-injection for acute allergic reactions
Neutralizing antibody titer (RFFIT >=0.5 IU/mL) in immunocompromised patients or high-risk lab personnel
